Pests arrive on new plants and through open windows, and by the time a
plant looks sick the colony is large. Spider mites leave fine webbing
between the stems and prefer dry air; mealybugs sit white in the leaf
axils like drops of cotton.

Every treatment opens the same way: isolate the plant, wash the leaves,
then repeat the spray after a week to catch the next hatch. A healthy
plant shrugs off what a stressed one dies of.
